title: ai-playbook bundle config (v1)
description: Declarative bundle produced by config-ui (HTML) and consumed by scripts/apply_config.py + scripts/bootstrap.py --from-config. Tri-category surface: rules{} (per-rule toggles + layers + advanced), features{} (installed components with state files + side effects — today only caveman), global_flags{} (binary env-driven toggles, no state file). Sparse: only modified-from-default entries appear. Sub-shapes are declarative intent only — the canonical state lives in per-feature files (.ai-playbook/rules-toggle.json, .ai-playbook/caveman.json, .ai-playbook/feature-flags.env), each gitignored.

generated_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the UI exported this bundle. Optional.

generated_by.description: Identifier of the agent/user that exported the bundle. Optional; UI defaults to 'anonymous' when no git user is detectable in-browser.

rules.description: Sparse map of rule-slug -> override. Same shape as schema-rules-toggle-v1.json's `rules` field; apply_config projects these into <consumer>/.ai-playbook/rules-toggle.json verbatim. Rules absent are inherited as fully-ON.

features.description: Installed features with their own state file + side effects. Only features explicitly modified appear here. apply_config delegates to each feature's CLI (e.g. `python -m scripts.caveman on/off`) to preserve materialisation + backups.

caveman.description: Caveman declarative intent. apply_config translates this to `python -m scripts.caveman on --mode X --components csv` or `off`. The canonical state lives at .ai-playbook/caveman.json (managed by the caveman CLI only; see schema-caveman-toggle-v1.json).

enabled.description: Master switch. When false, apply_config calls `caveman off` (strips AGENTS.md block + restores MCP wrappers).

mode.description: Intensity level for response_style. Consulted only when enabled=true.

global_flags.description: Binary env-driven toggles without their own state file. Keys come from config-ui/global-flags-inventory.json. apply_config projects these into <consumer>/.ai-playbook/feature-flags.env via the inventory's env_var/value_on/value_off mapping. Consumer must source the file in their shell init (direnv .envrc, bashrc, etc.) for the flags to take effect.

skills_enforce.description: Per-skill enforcement choices. Negative-list (opt-out) shape: only `disabled` is persisted in the bundle. apply_config projects this section into <consumer>/.ai-playbook-state/skills-enforce.json (schema: skills-enforce/v1), and scripts/materialise_skills.py honours it on next materialise pass. Omitted ⇒ all skills enforced (default).

disabled.description: Skill slugs (directory names under skills/) that MUST NOT be materialised on this consumer.

mcps_enforce.description: Per-MCP-server enforcement choices. Negative-list (opt-out): only `disabled` is persisted. apply_config projects this section into <consumer>/.ai-playbook-state/mcps-enforce.json (schema: mcps-enforce/v1), and scripts/mcp/render.py + scripts/mcp/validate.py honour it on the next render/validate pass. Omitted ⇒ all servers enforced (default).

disabled.description: MCP server canonical IDs (the `id:` field in mcp-servers*.yaml) that MUST NOT be rendered into `.mcp.json` or `.gemini/settings.json` for this consumer.

project_meta.description: Free-form project content rendered into AGENTS.md outside marker blocks. Persisted in the consumer's AGENTS.md as custom sections; this bundle entry is the transfer format only. Free-form Unicode text, line-broken as the user wrote it.

gitignore_extras.description: Consumer-added gitignore patterns. apply_config writes these to .gitignore OUTSIDE the playbook marker block. One pattern per line.

pre_commit_extras.description: Consumer-added pre-commit hooks. apply_config appends these to .pre-commit-config.yaml after the playbook-managed block. Each hook is a raw YAML object (validated structurally, not by pre-commit's own schema).

coderabbit_extras.description: Consumer additions to .coderabbit.yaml — extra path_filters and path_instructions. apply_config merges these with the playbook-canonical baseline.

claude_settings_extras.description: Consumer extras for .claude/settings.local.json (Claude Code natively merges this on top of settings.json). apply_config writes only this file; settings.json itself is canonical. LEGACY: prefer the model-agnostic `settings` key; entries here are still honoured and union-merged into `.claude/settings.json` permissions for backwards compatibility.

settings.description: Model-agnostic settings surface (the door's single source for agent-runtime config). Projected to .claude/settings.json via identity deep-merge (preserving every consumer-authored key) and, where the target supports it, to Gemini/Cursor. Each hook may carry an optional `targets` array to scope it to specific models; absent ⇒ all supported targets. The openspec-apply-enforce PreToolUse invariant is ALWAYS ensured by apply_config regardless of this section — presence of the key only signals that the door manages .claude/settings.json for this consumer.

hooks.description: Agent-runtime hooks to ensure (idempotent, deduped by command basename). Order-preserving; additive.

matcher.description: Tool/event matcher (Claude format). Omit for events without matchers.

targets.description: Models this hook applies to. Absent ⇒ all supported targets.

mcp_project_servers.description: Project-layer MCP server declarations. apply_config writes these into mcp-servers.project.yaml's `servers:` mapping. Keys are server IDs, values are full server records (passed through verbatim — validated by scripts/mcp/validate.py downstream).

manifest.description: block_id -> expected 12-hex SHA from _template_classifier.compute_sha. Updated by apply_config after each successful render.

file_states.description: Per-file render manifest. Key is the relative path (e.g. "AGENTS.md"). Lets the UI classify content as canonical / drifted on next load without needing the original template.

caveman_section_policy.description: Which free-form sections in project_meta caveman compresses on export. The AI-expert never-compress sections (§0/§2/§4/§5 in AGENTS.md, MCP server descriptions) are hardcoded in scripts/caveman/policy.py — this entry only controls the user-toggleable subset.

backup_preferences.description: UI-configurable backup behaviour. Read by apply_config and the migrate flow to decide where .bak files go and how many to keep.

location.description: next = alongside source file (user-visible). central = .ai-playbook-state/backups/. Default: next.

base_shas.description: Optimistic-concurrency tokens (compare-and-swap). Key is a managed-file relative path; value is the whole-file SHA (12 hex, \n-normalised) the config UI saw when it loaded files-state.js. apply_config recomputes the on-disk sha before writing each file and SKIPS it as a conflict when the value differs (the disk changed under the UI). Sparse/optional: files absent here are written without a CAS guard.

file_curate_intents.description: Per-file curate decisions captured by the config UI Files tab. apply_config reads these to decide whether to overwrite drifted blocks (default = take_playbook) or preserve the consumer's edited content (keep_mine). Keys are managed-file relative paths (e.g. "AGENTS.md").

default_action.description: Applies when a block's id is NOT present in `blocks` below. Default semantics: take_playbook (i.e. let the template content win). keep_mine preserves whatever is currently on disk for every block in the file.

blocks.description: Per-block override. Block id (e.g. "bootstrap-directive") -> action. Overrides default_action for that specific block.
